name: Math-VR
intro: Math-VR 是大规模中英双语数学视觉推理语料与基准。作者从约 90 万道含图解题中，经 Qwen2.5-VL-72B 筛图、GPT-4.1 转写和质检，先得到 89,075 道独立问题、178,150 条双语记录；再从 3,000 道候选题中人工保留 2,500 道测试题，展开为 5,000 条双语基准样本，并以答案正确性 AC 与过程部分得分 PS 评测。
org: The University of Hong Kong, Meituan, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
build_method: 公开题目收集, VLM图像筛选, GPT辅助标准化与质检, 专家人工复核
metric: AC（答案正确性）, PS（过程部分得分）
task_type: 开放式数学问答, 视觉推理
eval_feature: 视觉推理, 双语评测, 过程评分
variant: Paper bilingual corpus and benchmark; public English release
build_method_en: Public-problem collection, VLM image filtering, GPT-assisted standardization and quality checks, expert manual review
eval_feature_en: Visual reasoning, bilingual evaluation, process scoring
intro_en: Math-VR is a large-scale bilingual Chinese–English corpus and benchmark for mathematical visual reasoning. Starting from about 900K problems with illustrated solutions, Qwen2.5-VL-72B filters images and GPT-4.1 transcribes, standardizes, and verifies records, first yielding 89,075 unique questions and 178,150 bilingual records. Manual review then retains 2,500 test questions from a 3,000-question candidate pool; they expand to 5,000 bilingual benchmark items scored with Answer Correctness (AC) and Process Score (PS).

drawio_review_note: Source-only audit completed 2026-07-21 against Math-VR paper arXiv:2510.11718v1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11718v1), official HKU-MMLab/Math-VR-CodePlot-CoT snapshot 45b8c8885a12b172041a781ee45a13c48c56d401 (https://github.com/HKU-MMLab/Math-VR-CodePlot-CoT/tree/45b8c8885a12b172041a781ee45a13c48c56d401), public benchmark snapshot b15f5bb8454409c05dae801c235c7fc571689044 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/gogoduan/Math-VR-bench/tree/b15f5bb8454409c05dae801c235c7fc571689044), and public train snapshot 4c4361142039c44994cca92d6d3987442fc6c6f0 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/gogoduan/Math-VR-train/tree/4c4361142039c44994cca92d6d3987442fc6c6f0). The paper collects about 900K secondary-school problems whose solutions contain images from unspecified public websites; neither source URLs, crawl dates, deduplication method, filter thresholds, model snapshots, nor random seed are disclosed. Qwen2.5-VL-72B removes questions whose images are irrelevant or purely textual and retains mathematical figures required for reasoning. GPT-4.1 transcribes remaining text images, separates question and solution into Markdown, removes incomplete/incoherent records, and translates them to English. This construction first yields 89,075 unique questions and 178,150 Chinese/English language-specific records; the 86,575-train plus 2,500-test split is not frozen before benchmark selection. The paper then excludes proofs and most multiple-choice questions, randomly draws 3,000 candidates, asks GPT-4.1 for answer summaries and value-1-or-2 scoring points, and combines nontrivial-visual-reasoning selection with answer/rubric verification in one review by 15 senior STEM college students. After 2,500 questions are retained, the final paper split is 86,575 train plus 2,500 test; the test set contains 1,000 text and 1,500 multimodal questions, or 5,000 bilingual language-specific items. The v1 PDF is internally inconsistent about geometry share: the main text on p.4 and Appendix A.2 prose on p.14 report 81%, the Figure 3 caption on p.5 reports 77%, and the Figure 6 caption on p.14 reports 76%; the diagram preserves all three reported values and their pages. The released evaluator iterates only IDs supplied in answer.json and does not enforce 2,500-ID coverage; its GPT-4.1 judge receives question text, candidate response, answer summary and rubric but no question image. It slices text from the first left brace through the last right brace and applies json.loads only, with no schema or field-type validation; it retries at most five times and omits an ID after exhausted JSON-decode failures. summarize_score.py uses Python truthiness of is_fully_correct for PS, so any truthy value gives PS=100, but AC=100 only when the value is literally True via the identity test is True. Consequently, the JSON string "False" or number 1 yields PS=100 and AC=0. For a falsy value, AC=0 and PS=0.7 times final_score divided by max_score times 100, without type, clipping, or range validation. The script averages only keys present in result.json, separately for text, multimodal and overall, so missing answer IDs and exhausted judge IDs do not enter denominators; a stored JSON object missing expected scoring fields increments the denominator before the exception and therefore contributes zero. The paper's separate reliability study samples 1,000 questions and three model answers each; 15 students annotate 200 answers apiece, producing AC Cohen kappa/MCC 0.75 and PS Pearson 0.72/Spearman 0.70. Release drift is explicit: the pinned Math-VR-bench Parquet has 2,500 rows although its README table says text 1,000, multimodal 2,500 and total 3,000; the pinned Math-VR-train service reports 86,517 rows rather than the paper's 86,575. Both HF cards declare Apache-2.0 and the code repository declares MIT, but row-level public-website provenance and upstream reuse rights are not published. Formal drawio/SVG/PNG assets are intentionally outside this source-only edit. Formal publication evidence [site-a11r-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3572×865 (English) and 3565×865 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3570×863 and 3563×863. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
